ConnectionStrings.//: The control plane's OWN database — the tenant registry. List BOTH cluster nodes so it follows a failover; Target Session Attributes=Primary keeps writes off the standby.

Fleet.//DataNetwork: EMPTY on purpose — production has no data network, Postgres is off-box. A non-empty value makes ConnectNetworkAsync fail.
Fleet.//TraefikCertResolver: EMPTY on purpose — there is no ACME here. The Cloudflare Origin certificate is served from Traefik's default TLS store, so tenants need tls:true and no resolver.

TenantLogs.//: Farm Mongo. Empty URL = journal page answers disconnected (no 500). The user must read every logs_* database; tenant containers get their own user. Secret — not on the Settings screen.

TenantDatabase.//: Admin connection — used only to create and drop tenant databases and roles.
TenantDatabase.//Host: Both nodes: CREATE DATABASE must reach the primary, and Target Session Attributes is added automatically when this is a list.
TenantDatabase.//TenantHost: What the tenant container gets. Same list, so a provisioned tenant follows a failover exactly like a hand-deployed one.

Demo.//: Only the shared secret. Every demo POLICY knob is in the settings catalogue and editable in the panel; this one is a credential and stays in cp.env. Empty means the public demo endpoint refuses with 503 rather than accepting anonymously.

Billing.//: Stripe credentials only. Policy knobs (Enabled, TenantSlug, BankDetails, SweepIntervalSeconds) are in the settings catalogue. Empty keys hide card pay; bank still works.

Mail.//: Where the invitation comes from. Disabled means tenants are created but nobody is invited.

Docker.//: Empty = the local daemon. Point at a socket proxy in production (ControlPlane.Deployment.md §12).

Access.//: UNUSED when Directory is configured. Kept so an Access application can be rolled back without a code change. Unset these and delete the Cloudflare Access application for cp.zulo.one.

Directory.//: The public way in. login.getzulo.com is the identity provider; this process is the OAuth client `controlplane`.

Operator.//: The break-glass account, for when Cloudflare is what is broken. Reached over an SSH tunnel to BreakGlassPort, never from the internet.
Operator.//PasswordHash: A BCRYPT HASH, never a password. Storing the hash is what keeps this file merely sensitive rather than a credential. Changing it here also revokes every outstanding session.

Portal.//: The CUSTOMER portal at /portal — people who bought a stand, looking after it themselves. Nothing to do with Operator above: separate accounts, separate sessions, separate authorization policy.
Portal.//Enabled: FALSE by default, and turning it on is a decision about the EDGE, not just this file. The panel sits behind Cloudflare Access; customers are not staff, so Access must be told to BYPASS /api/portal and /portal or every customer is blocked before the request reaches here.
Portal.//PublicUrl: Where a browser reaches the portal. Every verification and reset link is built from THIS, never from the request's Host header — a link built from an attacker-supplied host is how account takeover by host-header injection works.
Portal.//ResetTokenMinutes: Short on purpose: this one is a password equivalent sitting in a mailbox.
Portal.//ClaimByAdminEmail: A newly confirmed address takes ownership of stands whose AdminEmail matches it. Turn OFF where stands are provisioned against a shared internal address — one account would claim the fleet.
